title: Maximum Points After Enemy Battles
summary: Given an integer array enemyEnergies representing the energy values of various enemies and an integer currentEnergy representing the initial amount of energy you have, you can perform the following operations to gain points: - Choose an unmarked enemy i such that currentEnergy is greater than or equal to enemyEnergies[i].
statement: Given an integer array enemyEnergies representing the energy values of various enemies and an integer currentEnergy representing the initial amount of energy you have, you can perform the following operations to gain points: - Choose an unmarked enemy i such that currentEnergy is greater than or equal to enemyEnergies[i]. By choosing this option, you gain 1 point and your energy is reduced by the enemy's energy, i.e., currentEnergy = currentEnergy - enemyEnergies[i]. - If you have at least 1 point, you can choose an unmarked enemy i. By choosing this option, your energy increases by the enemy's energy, i.e., currentEnergy = currentEnergy + enemyEnergies[i], and the enemy i is marked. The goal is to maximize the points by optimally performing these operations. Return the maximum points you can achieve.
constraints: enemyEnergies is nonempty and positive; currentEnergy is nonnegative.
An affordable unmarked enemy can be fought repeatedly for one point while spending its energy; alternatively, with a point, mark an enemy to gain its energy.
hints: If the cheapest enemy is initially affordable, keep it unmarked as a repeatable point source and convert every other enemy into energy.
The total spendable energy is initial plus all enemy energy except one minimum copy; divide by the minimum cost.
If initial<minimum return zero; otherwise floor((initial+sum-minimum)/minimum).
No point can be earned below the minimum; once affordable, every other energy can be harvested while one cheapest target remains, reaching the upper bound.
editorial: No point can be earned below the minimum; once affordable, every other energy can be harvested while one cheapest target remains, reaching the upper bound.

tests.explanation: Keep one minimum-energy enemy available, mark the others for energy, and fight the minimum repeatedly for three points.
No enemy is initially affordable, so no first point can be earned and the answer is zero.
